caption: A whole green pepper rests on a wire rack over a gas flame, and its skin blisters, puffs up and blackens where the flame touches it.

sa.check: A whole green pepper rests on a wire rack over a gas flame.
The skin blackens where the flame touches it.
The side away from the flame stays green and smooth.
The blistering comes first and the blackening follows.

pc.expect: The skin lifts away from the flesh in blisters that stay raised and char, while the pepper keeps its body.
pc.fail: The blisters sink back and the skin ends smooth; or the pepper's whole body collapses in a single frame; or the skin peels off as a rigid shell that keeps the pepper's shape; or the pepper melts and runs.

pc.expect: The blackening happens on the skin where the flame licks it and spreads from there; it never fades.
pc.fail: A blackened patch fades back to green; or the side away from the flame blackens while the flame's side stays green; or the rack changes colour rather than the pepper; or the whole pepper blackens at once while the flame licks one spot.

pc.expect: The pepper rests on the rack, the flame points upward at it and any juices run down to the rack or the hob.
pc.fail: The pepper lifts off the rack and hangs; or the flame points downward away from the pepper; or juices climb the pepper's side; or the flame hangs below the hob.

pc.expect: The blistering and the blackening only advance while the pepper is over the flame.
pc.fail: A blister flattens and rises again with the pepper still over the flame; or the blackening spreads and shrinks in turn; or the skin blisters before the pepper is over the flame; or the blisters move to the side away from the flame.

pc.expect: One pepper on one rack; the pepper stays one piece and the rack keeps its wires.
pc.fail: A second pepper appears; or the pepper vanishes; or the pepper passes through the rack's wires; or a wire vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The rack, the hob and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The rack changes spacing; or the hob's knobs move by themselves; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: The charring of the skin is the caption's asserted outcome; the chemistry of it is not judged, only that the darkening runs one way and appears where the flame touches.
